cards.meaning: More than is needed.
cards.example: The extra line on Ada's school form was redundant.

cards.meaning: Required for a particular purpose.
cards.example: A receipt is necessary to collect the uniform in Aba.

cards.meaning: Without any mistake or defect.
cards.example: Bisi gave a flawless talk at assembly.

cards.meaning: Having a fault or some room for improvement.
cards.example: The trader sold imperfect pots at a lower price.

cards.meaning: Made less worthy or respectable.
cards.example: Cheating debased the school competition.

cards.meaning: Raised in standing or quality.
cards.example: Her honesty elevated the standing of the market union.

cards.meaning: Easy to follow or understand.
cards.example: The route from the park to the Kano market was straightforward.

cards.meaning: Hard to follow because it has many parts.
cards.example: The fare rules at the bus park were complicated.

cards.meaning: Willing to consider new ideas or suggestions.
cards.example: The PTA was receptive to Ada's proposal.

cards.meaning: Openly opposed or unfriendly.
cards.example: A few traders were hostile to the new levy.

cards.meaning: Acceptance without protest, even when reluctant.
cards.example: The chair took their silence at the PTA meeting as acquiescence.

cards.meaning: Opposition to a change or demand.
cards.example: The fare rise met resistance at the motor park.

cards.meaning: A very large amount, often more than needed.
cards.example: A plethora of shirts crowded the small Aba stall.

cards.meaning: Too little of something to meet demand.
cards.example: The village had a shortage of water in March.

cards.meaning: Open and sincere speech.
cards.example: The principal thanked Amina for her candour at the meeting.

cards.meaning: Behaviour that deceives people or breaks their trust.
cards.example: The traders condemned dishonesty in measuring rice.

cards.meaning: Someone just starting a skill or activity.
cards.example: A novice joined the school chess club on Monday.

cards.meaning: Someone who practises an activity with trained skill or for a living.
cards.example: A professional repaired the clinic's generator in Enugu.

cards.meaning: So unlikely or extreme that it is hard to imagine.
cards.example: To the team, missing another Abuja tournament seemed inconceivable.

cards.meaning: Believable or worthy of trust.
cards.example: The teacher asked for a credible account of how the window broke.

cards.meaning: Only on the surface or lacking depth.
cards.example: The prefect made a superficial check of the classroom.

cards.meaning: Reaching far below the surface or into a subject.
cards.example: A deep discussion followed the film at our school.

cards.meaning: Careful to avoid unnecessary risk.
cards.example: The prudent trader kept money aside for transport.

cards.meaning: Giving too little attention to what you are doing.
cards.example: A careless runner dropped the baton in Kano.

cards.meaning: Letting light through while blurring what is behind it.
cards.example: A translucent sheet covered the market stall roof.

cards.meaning: Blocking light so you cannot see through it.
cards.example: The nurse put the medicine in an opaque bottle.

cards.meaning: An insulting word for someone thought to act foolishly.
cards.example: A pupil was warned for calling a classmate an idiot.

cards.meaning: Someone with exceptional skill or intelligence.
cards.example: The robotics club called Amina a genius after her repair.

cards.meaning: Very surprised and upset by something.
cards.example: We were shocked when the roof came off the school hall.

cards.meaning: Showing little or no worry about something.
cards.example: The trader seemed unconcerned about the drizzle in Aba.

cards.meaning: Willing and able to adapt to changes.
cards.example: The school was flexible about when lessons could resume.

cards.meaning: Unwilling to adapt or make exceptions.
cards.example: The Lagos club kept a rigid rule about late arrivals.

cards.meaning: Working well with little waste of time or effort.
cards.example: The nurse ran the clinic queue with efficiency.

cards.meaning: Failure to do a task with the skill it requires.
cards.example: The union blamed the delay on the contractor's incompetence.

cards.meaning: Unwilling to speak freely about something.
cards.example: Tayo was reticent about his plans after school.

cards.meaning: Inclined to talk a great deal.
cards.example: Our loquacious guide talked all the way to Badagry.

cards.meaning: Liable to change suddenly or become tense.
cards.example: The situation at the market became volatile after the argument.

cards.meaning: Free from disturbance, anger or excitement.
cards.example: The motor park was calm after the meeting.

cards.meaning: Extremely small in amount or size.
cards.example: Only an infinitesimal amount of dye went into the sample.

cards.meaning: Greater than usual in size or amount.
cards.example: The Kano stall received a large order for sandals.

cards.meaning: Showing no concern for another person's suffering.
cards.example: The callous reply upset the injured pupil.

cards.meaning: Caring about someone who is in distress.
cards.example: A compassionate nurse stayed with the frightened child in Aba.

cards.meaning: So brief that it sounds rude.
cards.example: A curt reply ended the discussion at assembly.

cards.meaning: Showing good manners toward other people.
cards.example: The polite passenger thanked the danfo driver.

cards.meaning: Cold or unfriendly in manner.
cards.example: The buyer gave the trader a frosty greeting.

cards.meaning: Warm and friendly in manner.
cards.example: The new prefect gave us a cordial welcome.

cards.meaning: Shockingly evil or cruel.
cards.example: The radio report described a heinous crime in the state.

cards.meaning: Deserving praise or approval.
cards.example: The students made a laudable effort to restock the library.

cards.meaning: After some delay or development.
cards.example: The danfo eventually reached Yaba.

cards.meaning: At the start of a situation.
cards.example: Initially, only three pupils signed up for the Kano club.

cards.meaning: An insulting term for ordinary people as a group.
cards.example: The teacher warned that calling people plebs could offend them.

cards.meaning: A small group with more status or power than others.
cards.example: The speaker said the policy mainly helped the elite in Abuja.

cards.meaning: Removed sewing stitches from something.
cards.example: The Aba tailor unpicked the hem to lengthen the skirt.

cards.meaning: Closed an opening with stitches.
cards.example: The tailor sewed up the tear in Chidi's uniform.

cards.meaning: A deep or lasting dislike.
cards.example: Sade had an antipathy to loud chewing in class.

cards.meaning: A feeling of fondness or warmth.
cards.example: The pupils spoke with affection about their former teacher.

cards.meaning: Made weaker or less effective.
cards.example: A series of illnesses debilitated the team before the Kano final.

cards.meaning: Given renewed energy or strength.
cards.example: The new coach invigorated our team before the final.

cards.meaning: Changing without a regular pattern.
cards.example: Erratic power interrupted our evening lesson in Enugu.

cards.meaning: Recurring in a steady or expected pattern.
cards.example: The school held regular meetings throughout the term.

cards.meaning: Too unclear or general to pin down.
cards.example: The note gave vague directions to the motor park.

cards.meaning: Easy to understand without guessing.
cards.example: Emeka gave clear directions to the new clinic.

cards.meaning: Shared by people in a group.
cards.example: The compound had a communal tap.

cards.meaning: Reserved for one person or a particular group.
cards.example: The head teacher spoke with the pupil in a private room.

cards.meaning: Stated something firmly as true.
cards.example: The witness averred that she had been at the market.

cards.meaning: Said that a claim was untrue.
cards.example: The trader denied that he had charged a higher price.

cards.meaning: Slightly unwell or unable to attend because of illness.
cards.example: The assembly was led by another teacher because Mr Bello was indisposed.

cards.meaning: In good physical condition.
cards.example: The nurse said the pupil looked healthy again.

cards.meaning: Doing well financially.
cards.example: The prosperous trader opened a second stall in Onitsha.

cards.meaning: Failing to get a hoped-for result.
cards.example: An unsuccessful sales campaign left the Aba shop with full shelves.

cards.meaning: Without treating something as important or serious.
cards.example: The coach told us not to take the league match lightly.

cards.meaning: With real attention to importance or consequences.
cards.example: The head teacher took the safety complaint seriously.

cards.meaning: Kind or careful in handling people or things.
cards.example: The nurse was gentle with the frightened child.

cards.meaning: Severe or needlessly rough in manner.
cards.example: The harsh reply silenced the class at once.

cards.meaning: Morally low or shameful.
cards.example: The head teacher called the cheating an ignoble act.

cards.meaning: Morally right and worthy of respect.
cards.example: Returning the lost purse was an honourable act.

cards.meaning: Causing intense distress.
cards.example: It was a harrowing journey through the flooded streets of Lokoja.

cards.meaning: Giving enjoyment or a good feeling.
cards.example: We had a pleasant trip to the market in Nsukka.

cards.meaning: Moves in quick, short steps.
cards.example: The little dog scurries across the school yard when it rains.

cards.meaning: Moves slowly and wastes time.
cards.example: Ngozi dawdles on the way to the motor park.
